subject: MeridianHealth: SDK auth & model-routing action plan

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: MeridianHealth post-call recap + immediate SDK/auth tasks

Thanks again for your time earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap and agreed next steps from Redwood's side so we have alignment before the technical workshop: 

High-level goal:
- Integrate Redwood inference into Meridian Health's clinician triage pipeline (low-latency chat + reranking for structured suggestions).

Primary integration touches we discussed:
- SDK & auth: customer SDK install + OAuth2 service-account flows (we support both API keys and short-lived mTLS tokens).
- Structured output / tool-calling: recommend using the structured-output schema for discrete actions (suggested schema attached in the proposal).
- Embeddings & reranker: embeddings for semantic search + light reranker for top-K scoring to reduce hallucination risk.
- Model routing & policy: routing by latency SLO (regional), cost tier for background batch reranks, and a fallback chain (smaller quantized model -> larger open LLM -> hosted fallback).

Immediate asks for Meridian (action items we agreed):
1) Share the expected 95th percentile latency target for API calls (p99 also helpful) and peak qps for triage endpoint.
2) Confirm whether procurement prefers Redwood-hosted API or Dedicated pool (affects auth + certificate flow).
3) Grant a read-only folder on Drive for architecture artifacts (we referenced a template).

What we'll deliver before the workshop (by Thu 11/5):
- Short architecture proposal (attachment: meridian-routing-proposal.pdf) with SDK install steps, recommended auth flow, example structured-output JSON, and a preliminary routing policy.
- Policy snippets (policy-snippets.yaml) showing latency/cost thresholds and fallback chains.

Proposed next step: 60-min technical workshop to walk the architecture and confirm routing policies — available slots attached in the calendar link.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Markus for the routing-policy specifics after you share the latency/QPS numbers.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa — really helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side before the workshop: 

1) Latency/QPS: Our target for the front-end triage path is 200ms median and 500ms p95. Peak expected concurrency for the pilot is ~40 qps, with a steady-state of 8–12 qps.
2) Procurement: we prefer Redwood-hosted API initially; if we move to Dedicated later we will need stricter KMS/HSM controls.
3) Drive access: I’ll create a Meridian Health integration folder and share it with your team by EOD tomorrow.

- On embeddings: we plan to use a 10k-document knowledge base; do you have recommendations for embedding dimensionality and storage pattern (Redis vs. vector DB)?

Also looping in procurement (procurement@meridianhealth.com) for timeline visibility.

Thanks Aisha — great details. Short answers inline and next steps below.

Auth/OIDC:
- Yes, Redwood supports short-lived OIDC tokens and scoped claims. For Hosted API we recommend short-lived JWTs minted by your identity provider; for Dedicated we support mTLS + short-lived certificates. We will add an example of a token exchange flow to the proposal.

Embeddings guidance:
- For ~10k documents we typically recommend 768–1024 dim embeddings depending on retrieval precision needs. If you are operating with sub-100ms retrieval SLA, use Redis vector store with approximate nearest neighbor (HNSW) and local caching; if you want full-powered semantic search with more flexible features (annotations, ops), a managed vector DB (e.g., Pinecone/Weaviate) is fine — we’ll include tradeoffs in the doc.

Routing & policy notes (summary):
- Primary route: low-latency region-local model (quantized L2 4-bit variant) with KV cache per-request for common prefixes.
- Cost-tier route: background reranks (off-peak) can use larger non-quantized models to improve quality at lower priority.
- Fallback chain: if regional pool saturates, fallback to cross-region pool in same continent; if that also fails, a lightweight hosted fallback (lower-cost open model) with degraded output indicators to the client.

Attachments: I’ve attached the architecture doc (meridian-routing-proposal.pdf) and a short policy YAML (policy-snippets.yaml).

Action items — what we’ll do now:
- Markus to draft concrete routing thresholds and an example policy file you can test.
- Schedule 60-min tech workshop — proposed times in the calendar link.
- Share a sample SDK quickstart and token-exchange snippet in the Drive folder once it’s shared.

Markus — could you add expected token TTL defaults and an example policy that maps p95 latency thresholds to routing decisions?

—
Vanessa

Subject: Re: MeridianHealth: routing policy draft + token defaults

Attaching a suggested policy snippet and token defaults (policy-snippets.yaml). Key points: 

- Token TTLs: issue short-lived access tokens with a 5 minute TTL for user-facing calls; refresh tokens for server-to-server service accounts with 1h TTL and proof-of-possession if using mTLS.
- Routing thresholds (example):
  - p95 <= 250ms -> route to region-local quantized L2 model pool (primary)
  - p95 > 250ms and <= 700ms -> route to cross-region pool (secondary)
  - p95 > 700ms -> degrade to hosted fallback model, return metadata flag (x-redwood-degraded: true)
- Cost-tiering: background reranks should be scheduled during customer-defined off-peak windows and routed to larger unquantized model pool with lower scheduler priority.
- KV caching & batching: recommend a 200ms batching window for background jobs; prefix cache TTL of 12h for common prompts.

A few open questions for Meridian:
1) Do you have a strict requirement for a metadata flag name for degraded responses (we used x-redwood-degraded)?
2) Any constraints on cross-region traffic for PHI? If PHI cannot leave the region, we need to plan Dedicated deployment in-region.

I’ve attached the YAML; Vanessa — please push this into the Drive folder and I’ll iterate based on Aisha’s answers.

—
Markus Klein
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
